body: Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board announced an independent investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang. Fox Business said the stock was down nearly 6% around noon.

In a statement on Sunday, the board said reports suggested Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Independent directors and outside counsel will oversee the inquiry. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

TechCrunch said the inquiry concerns Huang's relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data centre company, whom US intelligence believes was spying for China. In a letter to staff, Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife and said he would cooperate fully, Al Jazeera reported.
China's foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, rejected the spy allegations as a smear. Several US law firms said on Monday they were investigating possible claims for shareholders.

stories.say: Instagram will now use AI worldwide to spot teenagers who claim to be adults and move them into Teen Accounts with tighter limits, Meta said on Monday.
stories.stand: Instagram will use AI to spot teenagers who claim to be adults and move them into Teen Accounts with tighter protections.
body: Meta said on Monday it is expanding its AI age-detection technology to Instagram users worldwide. The system looks for signs that an account belongs to a teenager, even if the user gave an adult birthday.
Suspected teens are moved into Teen Accounts. These limit who can message them, hide harmful comments and make accounts private by default, TechCrunch reported.

The system first launched in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, and reached Brazil and the EU in May, The Next Web said. Meta is still rolling it out on Facebook and plans to bring it to Threads later this year.

In August Meta agreed settlements worth up to $18bn with almost every US state and territory, committing to better identify teens and children under 13. In Australia, Meta has also begun using Apple's age-range signal.

stories.head: M John Harrison, 81, becomes oldest winner of the Booker Prize
stories.say: M John Harrison won the Booker Prize in London on Monday for The End of Everything. At 81, he is the oldest winner in the prize's history.
stories.stand: The British writer won the £50,000 prize on Monday for The End of Everything, his 13th novel, chosen unanimously by the judges.
body: The British writer M John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize for The End of Everything. The award, worth £50,000, was presented at a ceremony in London on Monday.

At 81, Harrison is the oldest winner in the prize's history. The National reported that the previous record holder was Margaret Atwood, who was 79 when she shared the 2019 prize. ABC News said the Booker Prize Foundation's chief executive, Gaby Wood, called him the first winner to emerge from science fiction.
The book is his 13th novel. It follows a scavenger and his elderly aunt on the south coast of England, decades after a mysterious invasion has caused society to collapse.

The judges, chaired by Mary Beard, chose it unanimously from 163 entries. The panel also included Raymond Antrobus, Jarvis Cocker, Rebecca Liu and Patricia Lockwood. The shortlist included novels by Marlon James, Elizabeth Strout and Douglas Stuart.

stories.say: Robert Laffont plans to publish a novel in February whose first draft was produced with Anthropic's Claude, while Gallimard's parent group will screen manuscripts for AI.
stories.stand: Robert Laffont will publish a novel first drafted with an AI model, while the group that owns Gallimard plans to check submissions with AI-detection software.
body: The French publisher Robert Laffont will release Les Touches fantômes by Sébastien Bailly in February 2027. Journal du Geek reported that the first draft was produced mainly with Claude, the AI model made by Anthropic.

Bailly then reworked the manuscript through about 30 versions. He estimates that between 2% and 20% of the original text remains. The publisher says the book will open with a text explaining the process and close with an afterword on how it was made.

The Madrigall group, which owns Gallimard and Flammarion, is taking the opposite approach. From January 2027, manuscripts sent to its publishing houses will be checked with AI-detection software, Journal du Geek and Publishing Perspectives reported.
Publishing Perspectives said Robert Laffont's managing director, Frédéric Martin, opposes such detection software.

stories.stand: The Japanese monster film topped the weekend box office ahead of The Cat in the Hat, with the best North American debut for a foreign live-action film.
body: The Japanese film Godzilla Minus Zero took $31.6m in North American cinemas on its opening weekend of 6 to 8 November. Yahoo News reported that it was the largest opening in the region for a live-action foreign film, beating Hero's $17.8m.
The film is directed by Takashi Yamazaki and distributed in the US by Gkids with Toho. Rotten Tomatoes said it was the best opening ever for Gkids, and that the film had made $63m worldwide so far.
Warner Bros' animated The Cat in the Hat came second with about $20m. Drummer Boy opened third with $9.3m, according to Rotten Tomatoes.

stories.head: New Zealand comedian Dai Henwood dies aged 48
stories.say: The New Zealand comedian Dai Henwood, a regular on the panel show 7 Days, has died at 48 after about six years with bowel cancer, his management said.
stories.stand: The 7 Days panellist and TV host died at Auckland Hospital after living with bowel cancer for about six years.
body: The New Zealand comedian Dai Henwood has died aged 48, his management said. He died on Tuesday, New Zealand time, at Auckland Hospital, holding his family's hands.

Henwood had lived with bowel cancer for about six years. The Otago Daily Times said he was diagnosed with stage 4 bowel cancer in 2020 and went public in 2023. He had chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery.
He was a regular on the TV panel show 7 Days and also appeared on Taskmaster NZ. He hosted the New Zealand versions of Dancing with the Stars and Family Feud. He won the Billy T Award in 2002.
In 2025 he was made an Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to entertainment and charity fundraising, 1News reported. He is survived by his wife and two children.

She died on 4 November at a hospital in New York. Her family said she had fought a long battle with multiple sclerosis.
Smith began modelling in 1972 and was named Bloomingdale's Model of the Year in 1978. She modelled for Chanel and Versace, and for the label of her brother, the designer Willi Smith.

stories.head: Television guitarist Richard Lloyd dies aged 75
stories.say: Richard Lloyd, who co-founded the New York band Television and played on Marquee Moon, has died at 75, months after being diagnosed with bile duct cancer.
stories.stand: Lloyd, a founder of the influential New York band behind Marquee Moon, had been diagnosed with bile duct cancer in March.
body: Richard Lloyd, guitarist and co-founder of the New York band Television, has died aged 75. ITV News reported that the band confirmed his death on X on Saturday.

Lloyd had been diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a form of bile duct cancer, in March. Yahoo News reported that a fundraising page said tumours had spread to his liver. A Facebook post said he died peacefully at home.

Lloyd helped found Television in 1973. He played on all three of its studio albums, starting with Marquee Moon in 1977. The band was among the first punk acts to play the New York club CBGB's, and broke up after Tom Verlaine died in 2023.
Lloyd also released nine solo studio albums. Johnny Marr paid tribute, calling him a true inspiration.

body: The Korea Popmusic Industry Association has criticised a New York Times report on the contracts of the K-pop group NewJeans. In a statement on Monday it called the report a one-sided and biased assessment, Korea JoongAng Daily reported.

The Times reported last Thursday that the members' contracts lacked provisions protecting minors. The association said major agencies, including HYBE, give all trainees the government's standard supplementary agreement for minors.

It said those agreements cover sleep, education and rest, and that member companies have youth protection officers. It also criticised the disclosure of a contract at the centre of a continuing legal dispute.
HYBE and its label ADOR have said the contracts were legal and negotiated in good faith.

stories.say: Sweden has returned objects looted from the Kingdom of Benin in 1897 to Nigeria, and 77 items taken in grave robberies to a museum in La Paz, Bolivia.
stories.stand: Benin objects taken by British troops in 1897 were handed over in Lagos, and 77 items including a healer's skull went back to Bolivia.
body: Sweden's National Museums of World Culture have returned looted objects to Nigeria and Bolivia, The Art Newspaper reported. The handovers began last week.

At a ceremony in Lagos, 39 Benin objects were formally restituted to Nigeria's National Commission for Museums and Monuments, The Art Newspaper said. British troops looted them from the Kingdom of Benin in 1897. Six will stay in Sweden on a ten-year loan.
The Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, had announced the return and said it followed years of diplomacy, New National Star reported.

In Bolivia, 77 objects from the village of Niño Korin went to the National Museum of Archaeology in La Paz. They include the skull of a Kallawaya healer. The Swedish museums say the objects were taken in grave robberies in the 1970s.

body: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis has attended ceremonies in Serres marking the return of church treasures taken to Bulgaria in 1917.

Athens News reported that two silver liturgical fans with Byzantine enamels went back to the Monastery of St John the Baptist near Serres. They are among 48 church and historical items that Bulgaria transferred to Greece this autumn.

Mitsotakis called the return the correction of a historical injustice. Metropolitan Theologos of Serres and Nigrita thanked the government, Greek City Times reported.

stories.stand: The plan includes C$783.1m over five years for national cultural institutions and free entry to national museums for visitors under 25.
body: Canada's proposed federal budget includes C$783.1m over five years for national museums and cultural institutions, The Art Newspaper reported. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled the budget on 5 November.

The money would go to national museums, the National Arts Centre, Library and Archives Canada and the National Battlefields Commission. National museums would also become free for visitors under 25, at a cost of C$46.3m over five years.
Prime Minister Mark Carney said artists would not pay tax on up to C$45,000 of income from creative work. The government has not set the measure's cost, start date or eligibility rules.
The artists' body Carfac said the funding falls far short of what is needed.

stories.head: Norris wins wet São Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes clinch constructors' title
stories.say: Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen to victory at a rain-hit Interlagos on Sunday, while Mercedes wrapped up their first constructors' crown since 2021.
stories.stand: Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen at Interlagos on Sunday, and Mercedes secured their first constructors' championship since 2021.
body: Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos on Sunday. Max Verstappen was second for Red Bull, 14.602 seconds behind, and his teammate Isack Hadjar was third.
Mercedes clinched the constructors' championship with three rounds left, Sky Sports reported. It is their ninth title and their first since eight in a row from 2014 to 2021.

Kimi Antonelli, who won the drivers' title at the previous race in Mexico City, led early but spun at Turn 1 on lap 20. He finished fifth after a penalty for an unsafe release. George Russell was fourth.
Verstappen started 21st after grid penalties for engine parts. Rain returned late in the race. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finished eighth and ninth.

stories.head: Alcaraz beats Shelton to win his first Paris Masters title
stories.say: Carlos Alcaraz avenged his US Open defeat by Ben Shelton, winning seven-six, seven-five on Sunday for his first Paris title and ninth at Masters level.
stories.stand: Carlos Alcaraz won in straight sets on Sunday, avenging his US Open defeat by Ben Shelton before next week's ATP Finals in Turin.
body: Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton 7-6 (5), 7-5 in the Paris Masters final on Sunday. The match lasted 1 hour 57 minutes.

It was the Spaniard's first title in Paris and his ninth at Masters 1000 level, the ATP said. Shelton had beaten him in a five-set US Open quarter-final in September. "This one means a lot to me," Alcaraz said.
Alcaraz has won nine matches in a row, including the Vienna title, and has five tour-level titles this year. Only Jannik Sinner, with six, has won more.
Both players head to the ATP Finals in Turin, which run from 15 to 22 November. Sinner will miss the event through injury, Yahoo Sports reported.

stories.say: Aryna Sabalenka beat Karolina Muchova in two tight sets on Monday, and Mirra Andreeva thrashed Elina Svitolina on her debut, setting up a meeting between them.

body: Aryna Sabalenka beat Karolina Muchova 7-6 (2), 7-5 at the WTA Finals on Monday. Mirra Andreeva then beat Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0 on her debut at the event.
The tournament is being played at Indian Wells, California. Malay Mail reported it was moved from Saudi Arabia because of the regional war that followed US strikes on Iran.
On Sunday, Coco Gauff beat fellow American Jessica Pegula 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2. Linda Noskova, the Wimbledon champion, beat Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4, Arab News reported.
Kostyuk replaced world number one Elena Rybakina, who withdrew through illness. Sabalenka, twice a runner-up, faces Andreeva next and is chasing her first WTA Finals title.

body: England beat Australia 45-22 at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, on Sunday in the Nations Championship. RugbyPass said it was England's highest points total against Australia.
Henry Pollock, 21, scored twice after moving to the wing when Immanuel Feyi-Waboso went off injured. England led 19-10 at half-time.
Sky Sports said Feyi-Waboso hurt his right leg in a hip-drop tackle by Angus Bell, who was shown a yellow card. Seb Atkinson also went off with a hip injury.

stories.say: Scotland trailed by only three points at half-time, but New Zealand pulled clear after the break, and Beauden Barrett's double took him to fifty Test tries.
stories.stand: New Zealand scored seven tries and kept Scotland scoreless after half-time, with Beauden Barrett reaching 50 Test tries.
body: New Zealand beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield on Saturday in the Nations Championship. The All Blacks led only 24-21 at half-time, but Scotland did not score after the break.
Beauden Barrett scored twice, taking him to 50 Test tries. New Zealand scored seven tries in all. Hooker Ewan Ashman scored at least twice for Scotland from lineout drives.
Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu was sin-binned in the second half. Head coach Gregor Townsend said first-half indiscipline let New Zealand into Scotland's 22, and he questioned the card.
The All Blacks, coached by Dave Rennie, play Wales in Cardiff next.

body: Wales beat Japan 28-21 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Saturday in the Nations Championship. Josh Adams scored two tries, and Archie Griffin and Louis Rees-Zammit also crossed.
ESPN's match record shows Adams scored Wales's fourth try in the 70th minute. Japan replied through Ben Gunter, Warner Dearns and a late try from Kenta Fukuda.
RugbyPass named Rees-Zammit player of the match. Japan coach Eddie Jones said his side failed to take three chances inside the 22, and he questioned the refereeing at the breakdown.

stories.head: Sylhet Test drawn after Hridoy's record 242 for Bangladesh
stories.say: Towhid Hridoy's unbeaten two hundred and forty-two set a Bangladesh Test record, and Mushfiqur Rahim passed seven thousand Test runs as the Sylhet Test was drawn on Monday.
stories.stand: Bangladesh and West Indies drew the second Test on Monday, after Towhid Hridoy made Bangladesh's highest Test score and Mushfiqur Rahim reached 7,000 runs.
body: The second Test between Bangladesh and West Indies in Sylhet ended in a draw on Monday. Bangladesh were 184 for 4, chasing 369, when bad light halted play.

Towhid Hridoy's unbeaten 242 in the first innings was the highest Test score by a Bangladesh batter, ESPN reported. It beat Mushfiqur Rahim's 219 not out. Bangladesh had been 184 for 7 before recovering to 386.
On Monday, Mushfiqur became the first Bangladesh batter to reach 7,000 Test runs. For West Indies, Kavem Hodge made 142 in the second innings, his third Test century.

stories.head: Pakistan reach 281 for 5 with four debutants against Sri Lanka
stories.say: Debutant Tayyab Arif and captain Babar Azam made half-centuries as Pakistan reached two hundred and eighty-one for five on the opening day against Sri Lanka on Monday.
stories.stand: Sri Lanka chose to bowl under new Test captain Kusal Mendis, but Pakistan's batters had the better of the opening day in Rawalpindi on Monday.
body: Pakistan finished the first day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on 281 for 5 on Monday, ESPN reported. Bad light ended play after 67.2 overs.
Pakistan picked four debutants: Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, Arafat Minhas and Saqib Khan. Tayyab Arif made 57 from 51 balls, and captain Babar Azam scored 50.
Sri Lanka won the toss and bowled, picking four fast bowlers and leaving out spinner Prabath Jayasuriya. Kusal Mendis is captaining Sri Lanka in Tests for the first time.
Saud Shakeel was unbeaten at stumps. ESPN said Pakistan are bottom of the World Test Championship table and Sri Lanka are seventh.
